content:
Sean Gallagher: we need to lock the gate metrics + thresholds for safe apply. goal: stop bad rollout quickly, but avoid pausing every time p99 jitters.

Sean Gallagher: current strawman from kickoff: gate on 5xx rate + p95 latency + GPU saturation. question is thresholds + windowing + min volume.

Allison Grant: +1. also need to be explicit about tags/dimensions. if we can’t slice by `tenant/model/region/config_version` we’ll get nonsense gates.

Ethan Park: control plane side can attach `rollout_id` and `config_version` to the apply events + canary controller state. runtime can tag metrics with config_version as long as the workers know the active version.

Noah Patel: runtime can emit `redwood.runtime.active_opt_config_version` gauge + include `opt_config_version` label on request metrics. but careful: metric cardinality w/ per-tenant labels.

Allison Grant: for gating, we can keep labels to: tenant_id (hashed), model, region, config_version, rollout_id. we’re already doing tenant_id in a bunch of SLO dashboards. sampling may be needed but gates should run on unsampled.

Aisha Bello: what’s the expectation for “pause safely”? i’m worried about false positives (e.g. transient 5xx spike from unrelated deploy) causing gate to pause, leaving rollout stuck.

Sean Gallagher: proposal: gate failure => pause rollout (not rollback) by default. rollback is manual confirm (except maybe internal accounts). pause should be reversible + idempotent.

Paula Mendes: product-wise, pausing is fine as default. we should avoid auto-rollback for GA (we can add later). but we need clear criteria in Console copy: “Paused due to gate failure: X, Y. Click resume or rollback.”

Benji Okafor: implementation detail: canary controller will evaluate gate every N minutes per step and either (a) continue, (b) pause, or (c) hard-fail. we need gate rule definitions this week.

Allison Grant: ok, concrete suggestions:
- Error gate: HTTP 5xx rate for the canary slice compared to control slice (previous config_version) OR absolute SLO threshold.
- Latency gate: p95 only (not p99) to reduce noise.
- Saturation gate: GPU utilization + queue depth (scheduling latency) to catch batching heuristics blowing up.

Allison Grant: biggest question: compare to baseline or absolute? baseline is great but can be flaky with low traffic.

Sahana Iyer: from CI/e2e perspective, baseline compare is hard to simulate reliably. absolute thresholds are easier but might block legit high-latency tenants.

Aisha Bello: +1 on min request volume. we should not gate on 20 requests.

Jonas Weber: for quantization rollouts, we’ll also have eval/quality gates, but those are out-of-band from runtime metrics. still, we should align windows so rollout doesn’t progress before eval results land.

Sean Gallagher: sticking to runtime health gates in this thread. we’ll do a separate thread for eval gate windows.

Sean Gallagher: here’s a draft (numbers are placeholders):
1) 5xx gate: canary 5xx_rate > 0.5% for 5m AND at least 2x control 5xx_rate
2) latency gate: canary p95 > (control p95 + 75ms) for 10m OR > 1.25x control p95
3) saturation gate: GPU util > 95% AND queueing delay p95 > 50ms for 10m

Allison Grant: 0.5% 5xx is too high for hosted API. our steady state is ~0.05-0.1% depending on route. if we wait until 0.5% we’re already in customer pain.

Aisha Bello: agree. also “2x control” is weird when control is ~0.01% (noise). better to do absolute threshold + delta threshold.

Allison Grant: suggest error gate in burn-rate form:
- For canary slice, if error_rate_5xx > 0.2% over 5m AND > 0.1% over 15m => pause
- Require min_count: >= 500 requests in 5m (otherwise skip + extend step)

Benji Okafor: canary step durations are currently planned at 10m. if min volume isn’t hit, we can auto-extend step up to max (say 45m) then pause with “insufficient data”.

Sean Gallagher: ok. but do we want burn-rate w/ two windows for latency too?

Allison Grant: latency is trickier. absolute ms thresholds won’t generalize. relative to control is better.

Noah Patel: control p95 can shift due to traffic mix. if canary is 5% and gets a different prompt length distribution, we’ll gate incorrectly.

Allison Grant: yep that’s the false positive source. mitigation ideas:
- gate on “same route/model/region” (already)
- optionally gate on normalized latency per token? (we have `ms_per_output_token_p95` metric)
- require regression magnitude: p95 delta > max(100ms, 20%)

Aisha Bello: ms/token would reduce prompt length skew. do we trust that metric? does it include time-to-first-token vs streaming?

Noah Patel: we have both `ttft_ms` and `ms_per_output_token`. ms/token is only meaningful once streaming starts; ttft is impacted by caching/batching/kv. i’d propose:
- ttft p95 regression gate (relative)
- stream throughput regression gate (relative)

Sean Gallagher: feels like scope creep. what’s the minimum we can ship and not page ourselves to death.

Allison Grant: minimum: p95 end-to-end latency + 5xx. but we can define p95 as the route-specific metric we already use (`request_latency_ms_p95`).

Allison Grant: and we can add a “do not evaluate unless request_count >= N” to reduce noisy comparisons.

Benji Okafor: can the gate rules be expressed in slo-toolkit? i saw the PR adding a rule library.

Allison Grant: yes. we can start with something like:
```yaml
rules:
  - name: gate_5xx
    signal: http_5xx_rate
    windows: ["5m", "15m"]
    thresholds:
      - window: "5m"
        op: ">"
        value: 0.002   # 0.2%
      - window: "15m"
        op: ">"
        value: 0.001   # 0.1%
    min_requests:
      window: "5m"
      value: 500
    action: pause

  - name: gate_latency_p95
    signal: request_latency_ms_p95
    compare_to: control
    window: "10m"
    thresholds:
      - op: ">"
        value: 1.20    # 20% regression
      - op: ">"
        value_ms: 100  # OR +100ms
    min_requests:
      window: "10m"
      value: 1000
    action: pause
```

Sean Gallagher: this is good. question: do we make it “AND” or “OR” between relative and absolute?

Allison Grant: OR. if control p95 is tiny, 20% might be 10ms and noisy; absolute catches only meaningful deltas. if control p95 is huge, +100ms might be too lenient; relative catches real regressions.

Aisha Bello: can we add a “consecutive evaluations” requirement? i.e., must fail twice in a row before pausing?

Sean Gallagher: i like that. avoids pausing on one bad scrape.

Benji Okafor: easiest is: evaluate every 2m; if 2 consecutive fails => pause. if fail once then pass, reset counter.

Allison Grant: + annotate the gate decision with the values used (p95_canary, p95_control, req_count, etc). we’ll need it for oncall.

Paula Mendes: +1. that also helps with the Console copy (“Paused: p95 +28% vs control over 10m; 5xx 0.23% over 5m”).

Noah Patel: saturation: are we gating on GPU util? it’s a blunt tool and varies by model.

Aisha Bello: agree. i’d rather gate on queueing delay / scheduler latency (it’s directly correlated to user pain). GPU util can be high and still fine.

Allison Grant: ok: saturation gate becomes “queueing delay p95 > 30ms over 10m” (or “batcher_queue_ms”). but we need model-specific normal ranges.

Sean Gallagher: for v1, let’s keep saturation out of the hard gate, but alert on it. gating only on 5xx + latency p95.

Allison Grant: that’s acceptable as long as we still surface saturation panels in the rollout health dashboard. also, the alert thresholds can be looser.

Benji Okafor: works. controller supports multiple gate checks; we can make saturation gate optional per rollout config later.

Jonas Weber: note for quantization: latency can improve but quality can degrade. we should make sure “pause” semantics don’t automatically promote even if latency is better.

Paula Mendes: yep. promotion requires explicit action after canary completes + gates pass.

Sean Gallagher: false positive discussion: main sources are (a) low volume, (b) traffic mix skew, (c) unrelated incidents. mitigations we have:
- min volume + auto-extend step
- relative+absolute thresholds w/ OR
- consecutive failures
- show control vs canary and allow manual override w/ reason (audit log)

Aisha Bello: on (c), i’d add: if global incident / error budget burn is happening, pause new rollouts automatically? at least warn.

Allison Grant: we can add a “rollout freeze” flag later. for now, controller can check a simple signal: if region-wide 5xx > X, then block progression (pause with reason “region unhealthy”).

Benji Okafor: that’s easy-ish. i can add a preflight check per step: region health must be green. but we need the definition.

Sean Gallagher: definition: region health red if overall 5xx_rate > 0.3% over 5m OR p95 latency > 1.3x 7d median. (this is more for safety than correctness.)

Allison Grant: ok but careful with 7d median query complexity. maybe we do “vs last 30m” baseline for region health.

Noah Patel: +1. baseline queries across long windows will be expensive and slow.

Allison Grant: simplify: region health check = overall 5xx_rate > 0.3% over 5m (absolute) OR overall p95 > 2.0s over 5m (absolute). it’s crude but stops rollouts during fires.

Sean Gallagher: sold. that’s the “pause safely” part.

Paula Mendes: action items? i need something i can put in PRD as default gate behavior.

Sean Gallagher: summarizing defaults for GA:
- Gates evaluated per rollout step (every 2m)
- Pause if 2 consecutive evaluations fail
- Gate 1: canary 5xx_rate > 0.2% (5m) AND > 0.1% (15m), min 500 req / 5m
- Gate 2: canary p95 latency regression vs control over 10m: >20% OR >+100ms, min 1000 req / 10m
- If min volume not met: extend step up to 45m, then pause w/ “insufficient data”
- Preflight region health: if region-wide 5xx > 0.3% over 5m OR p95 > 2s over 5m => pause rollout before next step
- No automatic rollback in GA (manual rollback button)

Allison Grant: +1. i’ll wire these into the dashboard annotations + alert rules. also will add tags requirement doc: tenant/model/region/config_version/rollout_id.

Benji Okafor: i’ll update canary controller config defaults + add the consecutive failure logic.

Aisha Bello: can we ensure pauses page the operator? not full paging but at least Slack notification to #eng-oncall and a Console banner.

Sean Gallagher: yes. we can treat “rollout paused” as a non-paging alert routed to oncall Slack + incident-bot context.

Sahana Iyer: please tell me final thresholds today so i can bake into e2e expectations (we need deterministic pass/fail in staging).

Sean Gallagher: these are the finals unless someone objects by EOD. Allison can you post the YAML in the doc + link it here.

Allison Grant: will do. will also note we may tune once we see false positive rate in internal beta.

Paula Mendes: thanks all. i’ll reflect the “pause not rollback” default and the “insufficient data pause” in UX copy.

Sean Gallagher: cool. closing the loop after Allison posts the rule file.
